B1L10-G01-P226.title: Describe the following pictures with 跟.

scene.alt: Yuanzhen and her friend having tea and cake at a table.

repairs.note: 從 means “from” a place or time; the person you do something with takes 跟.
在 needs a place after it (在家); the person you do something with takes 跟.
Look at the picture: she is with her friend, not the shopkeeper.

items.fallbackRepair: 跟 + the person comes before the action: 元真跟朋友喝茶.

result.traditional: 元真跟朋友喝茶。
result.pinyin: Yuánzhēn gēn péngyǒu hē chá.
result.english: Yuanzhen has tea with her friend.

scene.alt: Yuanzhen buying a bag from the shopkeeper.

repairs.note: 給 + person means doing it for them; she buys from the shopkeeper: 跟老闆買.
從 means “from” a place or time; the person you buy from takes 跟.
She is the one paying, so she buys (買); selling is the shopkeeper’s job.

items.fallbackRepair: 跟 + the person you buy from, then the verb: 元真跟老闆買包包.

result.traditional: 元真跟老闆買包包。
result.simplified: 元真跟老板买包包。
result.pinyin: Yuánzhēn gēn lǎobǎn mǎi bāobāo.
result.english: Yuanzhen buys a bag from the shopkeeper.

scene.alt: Yuanzhen and the teacher in front of a blackboard.

repairs.note: 從 means “from” a place or time; the person you speak to takes 跟.
Look at the picture: it’s a classroom, so it’s the teacher, not a doctor.
叫 is for names (我叫…); to say words to someone, use 說.

items.fallbackRepair: 跟 + the person you speak to, then 說: 元真跟老師說.

result.traditional: 元真跟老師說：「你好！」
result.simplified: 元真跟老师说：「你好！」
result.pinyin: Yuánzhēn gēn lǎoshī shuō: “Nǐ hǎo!”
result.english: Yuanzhen says “Hello!” to the teacher.

repairs.note: 從 means “from” a place or time; the person you speak to takes 跟.
叫 is for names (我叫…); to say words to someone, use 說.
“你發燒了” is said to the sick person, so the doctor speaks: 醫生 first, 元真 after 跟.
“你發燒了” is said to the sick person, so the doctor speaks: 醫生 first, 元真 after 跟.

items.fallbackRepair: Speaker, 跟 + listener, then 說: 醫生跟元真說.

result.traditional: 醫生跟元真說：「你發燒了！」
result.simplified: 医生跟元真说：「你发烧了！」
result.pinyin: Yīshēng gēn Yuánzhēn shuō: “Nǐ fāshāo le!”
result.english: The doctor says to Yuanzhen, “You have a fever!”

repairs.note: 給 + person means doing it for them; to learn from someone, use 跟…學.
Mom is the one who can cook, so you learn from her (學); 教 is what she does.

items.fallbackRepair: The person you learn from goes after 跟, before 學: 我跟媽媽學做飯.

result.traditional: 會，我跟媽媽學做飯。
result.simplified: 会，我跟妈妈学做饭。
result.pinyin: Huì, wǒ gēn māma xué zuòfàn.
result.english: Yes, I learn to cook from my mom.

repairs.note: 得 follows a verb before a comment (說得很好); between a clause and its noun, use 的.
那是 already has its 是; 的 joins 我們上課用 to 書.

items.fallbackRepair: The whole clause comes first, then 的, then the noun: 我們上課用的書.

result.traditional: 不難，那是我們上課用的書。
result.simplified: 不难，那是我们上课用的书。
result.pinyin: Bù nán, nà shì wǒmen shàngkè yòng de shū.
result.english: No, it’s the book we use in class.

scene.alt: A man wearing glasses and a jacket with a fur collar.

repairs.note: 戴 is for glasses and masks; clothes take 穿.
得 follows a verb before a comment (說得很好); between a clause and its noun, use 的.

items.fallbackRepair: Clause, then 的, then the noun at the end: 他穿的衣服.

result.traditional: 很好看，他穿的衣服也很好看。
result.pinyin: Hěn hǎokàn, tā chuān de yīfu yě hěn hǎokàn.
result.english: They look good, and the clothes he’s wearing look good too.

scene.alt: A steaming bowl of beef noodles.

segments.traditional: 你喜歡吃他做的牛肉麵嗎？
segments.simplified: 你喜欢吃他做的牛肉面吗？

repairs.note: B doesn’t like his noodles, so the noodles B likes are someone else’s: 媽媽做的.
得 follows a verb before a comment (說得很好); between a clause and its noun, use 的.
是 can’t join a clause to a noun; 的 does: 媽媽做的牛肉麵.

items.fallbackRepair: Clause, then 的, then the noun: 媽媽做的牛肉麵.

result.traditional: 不喜歡，我喜歡吃媽媽做的牛肉麵。
result.simplified: 不喜欢，我喜欢吃妈妈做的牛肉面。
result.pinyin: Bù xǐhuān, wǒ xǐhuān chī māma zuò de niúròumiàn.
result.english: No, I like the beef noodles my mom makes.

segments.traditional: 愛唱歌的人一定愛聽音樂嗎？
segments.simplified: 爱唱歌的人一定爱听音乐吗？

segments.traditional: ，我妹妹愛唱歌，可是不愛聽音樂。
segments.simplified: ，我妹妹爱唱歌，可是不爱听音乐。

repairs.note: 一定 is negated with 不, not 沒.
都 means “all”; one sister who sings but doesn’t love music means “not necessarily”: 不一定.

items.fallbackRepair: 不一定 = not necessarily; 一定不 = definitely not. One example only shows “not necessarily”.

result.traditional: 不一定，我妹妹愛唱歌，可是不愛聽音樂。
result.simplified: 不一定，我妹妹爱唱歌，可是不爱听音乐。
result.pinyin: Bù yídìng, wǒ mèimei ài chànggē, kěshì bú ài tīng yīnyuè.
result.english: Not necessarily. My younger sister loves singing but doesn’t love listening to music.

segments.traditional: 常常上網的學生都不喜歡看書嗎？
segments.simplified: 常常上网的学生都不喜欢看书吗？

segments.traditional: 都很愛上網，也都很喜歡看書。
segments.simplified: 都很爱上网，也都很喜欢看书。

repairs.note: 得 follows a verb before a comment (說得很好); between a clause and its noun, use 的.
是 can’t join a clause to a noun; 的 does: 我教的學生.

items.fallbackRepair: Clause first, then 的, and the noun last: 我教的學生 (not 學生我教的).

result.traditional: 不是，我教的學生都很愛上網，也都很喜歡看書。
result.simplified: 不是，我教的学生都很爱上网，也都很喜欢看书。
result.pinyin: Bú shì, wǒ jiāo de xuéshēng dōu hěn ài shàngwǎng, yě dōu hěn xǐhuān kàn shū.
result.english: No. The students I teach all love going online, and they all like reading too.

segments.traditional: 喜歡去海邊游泳的人不怕曬太陽嗎？
segments.simplified: 喜欢去海边游泳的人不怕晒太阳吗？

repairs.note: 沒 can’t answer the question or negate 怕: agree with 對, then 不怕.
They love the sun, so they aren’t afraid of it: 對，他們不怕.
They aren’t afraid, which agrees with “不怕…嗎”, so start with 對.

items.fallbackRepair: Agree with the question first (對), then 不怕.

result.traditional: 對，他們不怕，也很喜歡曬太陽。
result.simplified: 对，他们不怕，也很喜欢晒太阳。
result.pinyin: Duì, tāmen bú pà, yě hěn xǐhuān shài tàiyáng.
result.english: Right, they aren’t afraid, and they love being in the sun too.

scene.alt: Two girls at a table with cake and small pastries.

segments.traditional: 她們吃的這些點心，你也想吃嗎？
segments.simplified: 她们吃的这些点心，你也想吃吗？

repairs.note: 得 follows a verb before a comment (說得很好); between a description and its noun, use 的.
是 can’t join a description to a noun; 的 does: 太甜的東西.

items.fallbackRepair: The description (太甜) comes first, then 的, then the noun: 太甜的東西.

result.traditional: 不想，我不喜歡吃太甜的東西。
result.simplified: 不想，我不喜欢吃太甜的东西。
result.pinyin: Bù xiǎng, wǒ bù xǐhuān chī tài tián de dōngxi.
result.english: No, I don’t like food that’s too sweet.

scene.alt: Two girls at a table with cake and small pastries.

segments.traditional: 穿紅衣服的那個女孩子是姊姊還是妹妹？
segments.simplified: 穿红衣服的那个女孩子是姐姐还是妹妹？

repairs.note: 得 follows a verb before a comment (說得很好); between a clause and its noun, use 的.
The girl in red is 姊姊, so 妹妹 is the one not wearing red, joined by 的: 沒穿紅衣服的那個.

items.fallbackRepair: The clause (沒穿紅衣服) comes first, then 的, then 那個.

result.traditional: 是姊姊，沒穿紅衣服的那個是妹妹。
result.simplified: 是姐姐，没穿红衣服的那个是妹妹。
result.pinyin: Shì jiějie, méi chuān hóng yīfu de nàge shì mèimei.
result.english: She’s the older sister; the one not wearing red is the younger sister.

segments.traditional: 她們穿的這兩件衣服都是媽媽做的嗎？
segments.simplified: 她们穿的这两件衣服都是妈妈做的吗？

repairs.note: 戴 is for glasses and masks; clothes take 穿.
Clothes are counted with 件: 那件.

items.fallbackRepair: Clause, then 的, then 那件: 姊姊穿的那件.

result.traditional: 不是，姊姊穿的那件是買的。
result.simplified: 不是，姐姐穿的那件是买的。
result.pinyin: Bú shì, jiějie chuān de nà jiàn shì mǎi de.
result.english: No, the one the older sister is wearing was bought.

repairs.note: Too thin means eating more, not less: 多吃.
很 goes before a state verb (很瘦); “more” before an action is 多.
太 means “too” (太瘦了); “more” before an action is 多.

items.fallbackRepair: 多 goes before the verb: 多吃一點兒.

result.traditional: 你太瘦了，應該要多吃一點兒。
result.simplified: 你太瘦了，应该要多吃一点儿。
result.pinyin: Nǐ tài shòu le, yīnggāi yào duō chī yìdiǎnr.
result.english: You’re too thin; you should eat a bit more.

segments.traditional: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，應該
segments.simplified: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，应该

repairs.note: Too much coffee means drinking less, not more: 少喝.
To cut down, not stop, use 少: 少喝一點兒.
很 goes before a state verb; “less” before an action is 少.

items.fallbackRepair: 少 goes before the verb: 少喝一點兒.

result.traditional: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，應該少喝一點兒。
result.simplified: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，应该少喝一点儿。
result.pinyin: Nǐ píngcháng hē tài duō kāfēi le, yīnggāi shǎo hē yìdiǎnr.
result.english: You usually drink too much coffee; you should drink a bit less.

repairs.note: 多 goes before an action (a verb), not a thing.
少 goes before an action (a verb), not a thing.

items.fallbackRepair: The exam is coming: study more (多看書) and go online less (少上網).

result.traditional: 快要考試了，你要多看書，少上網。
result.simplified: 快要考试了，你要多看书，少上网。
result.pinyin: Kuài yào kǎoshì le, nǐ yào duō kàn shū, shǎo shàngwǎng.
result.english: The exam is coming; you should read more and go online less.

repairs.note: Being tired all the time calls for more sleep, not less: 多睡覺.
Before a verb, “more” is plain 多: 多睡覺, not 很多睡覺.
太 means “too”; “more” before an action is 多.

items.fallbackRepair: 多 goes before the verb: 多睡覺.

result.traditional: 你應該多睡覺。
result.simplified: 你应该多睡觉。
result.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō shuìjiào.
result.english: You should sleep more.

scene.alt: An MRT train; two women talk below it.

segments.traditional: 明天你要怎麼去老師家？
segments.simplified: 明天你要怎么去老师家？

repairs.note: 在 + verb means doing it right now; for tomorrow use 會.
騎 is for bikes and scooters; you ride inside the MRT: 坐.
Look at the picture: it’s the MRT, not a bus.

items.fallbackRepair: Time, then 會, then how you go: 我明天會坐捷運去.

result.traditional: 我明天會坐捷運去。
result.simplified: 我明天会坐捷运去。
result.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì zuò jiéyùn qù.
result.english: I’ll take the MRT tomorrow.

scene.alt: A sick girl in bed with water and medicine beside her.

segments.traditional: 今天晚上大家可以吃很多好吃的東西，她會來嗎？
segments.simplified: 今天晚上大家可以吃很多好吃的东西，她会来吗？

repairs.note: Tonight hasn’t happened yet; “won’t” is 不會, not 沒.
很會 means “good at”; she’s sick, so she won’t come: 不會來.

items.fallbackRepair: 不 goes before 會, then the verb: 不會來.

result.traditional: 她生病了，不會來。
result.simplified: 她生病了，不会来。
result.pinyin: Tā shēngbìng le, bú huì lái.
result.english: She’s sick; she won’t come.

scene.alt: Weather forecast: today sunny 0%, tomorrow rain 50%, the day after rain 90%.

segments.traditional: 後天我們要去打棒球，會下雨嗎？
segments.simplified: 后天我们要去打棒球，会下雨吗？

repairs.note: B moves the game to today, so it will rain on 後天: 會.
The question is what will happen, so answer with 會.
能 is about being able to; the question is what will happen: 會.

items.fallbackRepair: Answer a 會 question with 會 or 不會.

result.traditional: 會，我們今天去吧！
result.simplified: 会，我们今天去吧！
result.pinyin: Huì, wǒmen jīntiān qù ba!
result.english: It will. Let’s go today!

B1L10-G05-P237.title: Answer the following questions with 要是/如果……，就……

segments.traditional: 要是你有很多錢，你想做什麼？
segments.simplified: 要是你有很多钱，你想做什么？

repairs.note: The “if” part takes 要是, and the result takes 就; 所以 is for a real result.
B answers about themself: 我.
With a lot of money you’d buy, not sell: 買.

items.fallbackRepair: 要是 + subject + condition, then 就 + result: 要是我有很多錢，就買大房子.

result.traditional: 要是我有很多錢，就買大房子。
result.simplified: 要是我有很多钱，就买大房子。
result.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ yǒu hěn duō qián, jiù mǎi dà fángzi.
result.english: If I had a lot of money, I’d buy a big house.

alternatives.traditional: 我要是有很多錢，就買大房子。
alternatives.simplified: 我要是有很多钱，就买大房子。
alternatives.pinyin: Wǒ yàoshi yǒu hěn duō qián, jiù mǎi dà fángzi.
alternatives.english: If I had a lot of money, I’d buy a big house.

segments.traditional: 如果你的手機不能上網，你會怎麼做？
segments.simplified: 如果你的手机不能上网，你会怎么做？

repairs.note: The “if” part starts with 如果, and the result takes 就; 所以 is for a real result.
The phone can’t go online, so use something else: 用電腦.

items.fallbackRepair: 如果 + condition first, then 就 + what you’d do: 就用電腦.

result.traditional: 如果我的手機不能上網，就用電腦。
result.simplified: 如果我的手机不能上网，就用电脑。
result.pinyin: Rúguǒ wǒ de shǒujī bù néng shàngwǎng, jiù yòng diànnǎo.
result.english: If my phone couldn’t go online, I’d use a computer.

segments.traditional: 要是你想多練習中文，你會怎麼做？
segments.simplified: 要是你想多练习中文，你会怎么做？

segments.traditional: 要是我想多練習中文，就
segments.simplified: 要是我想多练习中文，就

repairs.note: To practise more you speak more, not less: 多.
給 + person means doing it for them; to speak with someone, use 跟.

items.fallbackRepair: 就, then 多 and 跟朋友 before 說: 就多跟朋友說中文.

result.traditional: 要是我想多練習中文，就多跟朋友說中文。
result.simplified: 要是我想多练习中文，就多跟朋友说中文。
result.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ xiǎng duō liànxí Zhōngwén, jiù duō gēn péngyǒu shuō Zhōngwén.
result.english: If I want to practise Chinese more, I’ll speak Chinese with friends more.

alternatives.traditional: 要是我想多練習中文，就跟朋友多說中文。
alternatives.simplified: 要是我想多练习中文，就跟朋友多说中文。
alternatives.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ xiǎng duō liànxí Zhōngwén, jiù gēn péngyǒu duō shuō Zhōngwén.
alternatives.english: If I want to practise Chinese more, I’ll speak more Chinese with friends.

segments.traditional: 明天要是下雨，你要去海邊嗎？
segments.simplified: 明天要是下雨，你要去海边吗？

repairs.note: Tomorrow hasn’t happened; a plan not to go takes 不, not 沒.
要是 pairs with 就, not 所以.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 goes after the subject, right before 不 + verb: 我就不去了.

result.traditional: 要是下雨，我就不去了。
result.pinyin: Yàoshi xià yǔ, wǒ jiù bú qù le.
result.english: If it rains, I won’t go.
